title: A Salt for the Thorn Anew
premise: Elodie Ravensworth, the last swordspeaker whose oaths can bind steel to truth, has survived a decade of hiding by guiding smugglers through the Thornfell mountains. When Queen Marenne declares a kingdom-wide hunt for the gifted, Elodie's found family of smugglers is captured as bait, forcing him into the open. He learns that the old kingdom of Thornfell—erased from maps and law—left behind a door that opens only for an oath freely spoken, and it will close when the moon completes its thirteenth turn. In the end, Elodie must choose between using his gift's full corrupting power to save his family and speaking one final, self-annihilating oath that frees them, dissolves the hunt, and sends him beyond the door into exile.
about_author: Edmund Montrose is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent years mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy about borders, oaths, and the people who live in the gaps between them.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon Rises
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. He guides a smuggler caravan through Thornfell's hidden passes while concealing the oath-scar on his palm. A royal proclamation nailed at the pass announces the hunt for swordspeakers. The emotional beat is quiet dread: the life he built on invisibility begins to crack as he realizes the crown knows someone with the gift still walks these mountains.

chapters.title: A Family of Liars
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, with interludes from smuggler captain Sera Voss. At the smugglers' haven of Greyhollow, we meet his found family: Sera, the deaf tracker Bram, and orphaned apprentice Wren who suspects his secret. Warmth and banter establish what he stands to lose. The beat is belonging shadowed by guilt—he has lied to the people he loves most.

chapters.title: The Queen's Hounds
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Hale's POV. Hale, a former swordspeaker who betrayed her own kind, arrives in Thornfell with writs and soldiers. She interrogates villagers and reconstructs Elodie's old identity from court records. The beat is chilling competence: she is sympathetic, methodical, and utterly convinced that the gift must be extinguished for justice to exist.

chapters.title: What Oaths Cost
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, flashback-heavy. When bandits ambush a caravan, Elodie breaks his silence and speaks a binding oath to save Wren, feeling the gift's intoxicating pull—the more power he draws, the less he trusts his own motives. The beat is corruption's first taste: he saves everyone but frightens himself, and Wren sees his scarred palm.

chapters.title: The Map That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confronts Elodie, and instead of betrayal offers help: her grandmother's stories speak of a door out of Thornfell, the erased kingdom, openable only by a true oath before the thirteenth moon fills. They decode fragments hidden in old boundary stones. The beat is hope kindled between two liars learning to trust.

chapters.title: Greyhollow Burns
chapters.summary: Alternating Elodie and Sera POV. Hale tracks them to Greyhollow; the haven is raided and Sera, Bram, and the others are taken as declared bait, with a public promise of trial—and execution—for anyone harboring a swordspeaker. Elodie escapes with Wren. The beat is grief and rage: his invisibility has cost his family everything.

chapters.title: Bargains with Traitors
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Desperate, Elodie seeks out Hale alone and offers a bargain: himself in exchange for the prisoners' freedom. Hale reveals the truth of her fall—her own oath once enslaved her to a corrupt lord—and warns him the gift always takes more than it gives. The beat is uneasy kinship between two survivors of the same wound.

chapters.title: The Door in the Boundary Stone
chapters.summary: Elodie and Wren's POV. Following the decoded stones to the heart of old Thornfell, they find the door—a seam in a cliff that answers only to an oath freely spoken. But the door demands a price: the speaker's bond to the world he leaves. Meanwhile the moon nears full. The beat is awe curdling into dread as Elodie understands what 'out' truly means.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, climax. Rather than flee, Elodie returns under the full thirteenth moon to the queen's tribunal, where his family stands condemned. He speaks a final binding oath—not of power over others, but of witness—that forces the court to hear recorded truths of the hunt's atrocities, shattering its legitimacy. The strain unmakes his gift forever. The beat is sacrifice transmuted into justice outside the law.

chapters.title: A Salt for the Thorn Anew
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, resolution. The hunt collapses; Hale resigns rather than enforce a discredited writ, and the prisoners walk free. Salt is scattered on Thornfell's paths—an old rite marking a beginning, not an ending. At the boundary stone, Elodie, giftless and free, chooses to stay rather than pass through the door. The beat is quiet homecoming: family chosen, power refused, and a country remade one honest word at a time.
